sources.title: Tokummia katalepsis
sources.source_type: Primary museum taxon account, fossil photographs and curatorial reconstruction
sources.locator: Taxonomy; Type Specimens; Age & Localities; Description/Morphology and Maximum Size; Ecology. Gallery: ROMIP 63823, ROMIP 63826 and Danielle Dufault reconstruction.
sources.supports: Taxon, Wuliuan locality, maximum size, shell/head/trunk/tail structure and ecological interpretation.
sources.visual_inspection: Actual full-resolution images inspected: 2560 px holotype and paratype photographs and Dufault illustration, not merely captions or thumbnails. Photographs support external preserved structure; living depth and color are not measured.
sources.rights: Photographs and reconstruction remain copyright ROM/credited creators. Private research only; no copied pixels, scans or meshes enter the asset.

sources.title: Tokummia, a new fossil species from the Burgess Shale traces origin of ants, millipedes and lobsters.
sources.author: Cedric Aria
sources.source_type: Primary researcher museum account with specimens and technical reconstruction
sources.locator: ROM63826 image/caption; pincer description following it; holotype before/after-preparation captions; Technical drawings of Tokummia katalepsis by Danielle Dufault.
sources.supports: Contrasting preserved orientations; two terminal teeth on fixed pincer finger, curved opposing finger; limb classes, forked tail and interpreted mouthparts.
sources.visual_inspection: Actual 800x618 technical drawing inspected. Side reconstruction shows covered trunk and posterior limb series; ventral anterior drawing distinguishes antennae, mouthparts, pincers and walking limbs. Drawing is interpretive, not a dimensional blueprint.
sources.rights: Danielle Dufault / Jean-Bernard Caron, copyright ROM. Consulted privately; not incorporated or redistributed with the model.

sources.title: Paleontologists trace origin of millipedes, crabs and insects to new 508 million-year-old sea creature with can opener-like pincers
sources.source_type: Primary institutional report of Aria and Caron 2017 with life reconstruction
sources.locator: Lars Fields 3D reconstruction and caption; paragraphs on extended size, anterior legs, carapace, mandibles, pincers and lack of a second antenna.
sources.supports: Extended size over 10 cm, near-bottom ecology, specialized pincers and original head interpretation. Specific prey and behavior remain hypotheses.
sources.visual_inspection: Actual 500x285 reconstruction image inspected for shell/body/limb spatial relationship only. It is not fossil evidence or a source mesh.
sources.rights: Lars Fields, copyright ROM. Consulted-only image; no copied geometry, palette or texture.

use_note: Public-ready asset package contains citations only. Museum photographs, illustrations and page snapshots are isolated in private source provenance outside the deliverable tree. Scientific facts guide original geometry; artistic choices and uncertainty remain explicit.
